first_impression.reaction: My assistant read it, not me. The first screen is a legal and weather explainer, so it reads like a guide for any couple, not for a family planning for 300 guests. She only kept going because of the line about keeping the day private, and her summary came down to the venue questions near the end. The tone is calm and not pushy, which I like. But nothing on the first screen says this team has done a wedding my size.

journey.quote: This guide covers what sits behind that picture, from the paperwork to the questions that keep your day private.
journey.reaction: Privacy, mentioned early. This is the only reason the summary reached me at all.

journey.quote: Weddings here are usually planned around a hotel, with the ceremony, reception and guest rooms held in one place, and that shapes everything from the guest experience to how private your day feels.
journey.reaction: Honest. It tells me straight away that privacy at a resort is something you have to fight for. Useful to know.

journey.section: Resort, private estate or beach club
journey.quote: The right choice depends on how many guests you are bringing and how much of the property you want to yourselves.
journey.reaction: This is the part that matters most to us, and it gets one line. With 200 to 400 guests, the question is whether a property can be closed to the public, not which of three types I like.

journey.quote: Apostilles, translations and legalisation each take time, and they happen in sequence.
journey.reaction: Fine, but our lawyers and the family office deal with this. Pages of document steps feel like over-explaining for someone at my level, and most of it is written for Australian registries.

journey.quote: Mean daily highs move within a narrow band, from 27.6°C in February to 30.9°C in September.
journey.reaction: More detail than I need. My assistant skipped this part.

journey.section: Entry, tourist card and travel advice
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller's advice for the Dominican Republic is to exercise a high degree of caution, due to the threat of violent crime.
journey.reaction: Good that it's said plainly. It's also exactly why I would expect to read something about security for a family like mine, and there is nothing.

journey.quote: Use official airport taxis, ride share or hotel transport, never unofficial taxis, and travel to and from the airport in daylight.
journey.reaction: Ride share. This is written for regular tourists. Our guests will not be getting taxis.

journey.section: Other weddings that day and exclusive use
journey.quote: If you want the setting to yourselves, ask what exclusive use of each space covers, and for how many hours.
journey.reaction: Right question, but it stops at each space and a few hours. My question is whether the whole property can be ours for the full celebration.

journey.quote: Ask whether other hotel guests can use that stretch of beach during your ceremony.
journey.reaction: Yes. Strangers with phones on the beach is my real fear. I'd want the next question too: who is allowed to photograph or post.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and works in your time zone with quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quotes in AUD and your time zone assume I'm in Australia. I'm in Dubai. Having it in writing is good though.

journey.quote: Do Punta Cana resorts offer wedding packages?
journey.reaction: Package language. The answer is sensible, but seeing the word in a heading puts the page in the standard client category for me.

journey.quote: A Punta Cana wedding rewards the couple who decides early: legal or symbolic, drier months or not, and which venue will give the day to you alone.
journey.reaction: Understated and confident. 'To you alone' is the right note. This is the best line on the page for me.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests, here or anywhere? The page never says.
Can a whole resort or estate in Punta Cana be closed to the public for several days?
How do you work with a family's private security team and the venue's security?
What do you do to stop guests, staff or vendors leaking photos or details to press or social media?
Do you arrange private arrivals for VIP guests, or is that left to the family?
Is there a private or referral-only way to speak to someone senior, rather than a general enquiry form?
Can you plan for family customs and catering needs, for example halal kitchens or separate events?

turn_offs_found.quote: Use official airport taxis, ride share or hotel transport, never unofficial taxis, and travel to and from the airport in daylight.
turn_offs_found.why: This is written for regular tourists. It tells me who the page is really for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Do Punta Cana resorts offer wedding packages?
turn_offs_found.why: Package language in a heading. I don't want to be one of a dozen weddings on a resort's calendar.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and works in your time zone with quotes in AUD.
turn_offs_found.why: It assumes I'm an Australian couple on an Australian budget. Not a deal breaker, but it tells me this isn't written for me.

would_share_with: My assistant, to keep the exclusive-use and beach questions on file for venue calls

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, begin with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire from a blog post. If someone we know recommends Wedded Wonderland, this page wouldn't put me off, and the privacy questions would count in its favour. But nothing here tells me they've done a wedding my size, or that there is a private way to get in touch.

top_3_changes: Exclusive use: replace old "If you want the setting to yourselves, ask what exclusive use of each space covers, and for how many hours." with new "If you want the setting to yourselves, ask what exclusive use of each space covers, for how many hours, and whether it can extend to the whole property across your celebration." This turns the scale question I care about into a question for the venue, without promising anything.

Beach privacy: replace old "Ask whether other hotel guests can use that stretch of beach during your ceremony." with new "Ask whether other hotel guests can use that stretch of beach during your ceremony, and what the venue's policy is on guests and staff photographing or posting your wedding." Leaks are my biggest fear, and this shows the writer has thought about it.

Choosing a setting: replace old "The right choice depends on how many guests you are bringing and how much of the property you want to yourselves." with new "The right choice depends on how many guests you are bringing, how much of the property you want to yourselves and how private the days around the wedding need to be." Privacy over several days, not just the ceremony, is what separates my wedding from a standard one.

The scale and security gaps (unanswered questions 1, 3 and 5) can't be filled without brand evidence. Should they go to Nic rather than become draft edits?
